create.name: Jay Vidyarthi
create.bio:
Jay Vidyarthi is a Canadian meditation teacher and designer whose work sits where contemplative practice meets everyday technology. He has meditated since 2008 and has trained with teachers from Unified Mindfulness, in which he is certified to teach, and has also studied with monastics and teachers linked to the Monastic Academy, the Mind & Life Institute and Vipassana International. His teaching is secular and practical, built around open presence, clear seeing of emotions and an easy, unforced kind of awareness. Alongside it he runs Still Ape, a small studio that has helped design meditation apps, retreat-booking tools and other wellbeing products.

His book Reclaim Your Mind sets out seven ways to keep the good parts of phones, games and social media while drawing kinder boundaries around the rest, without shame about screen time. He calls himself an attention activist and teaches through guided practices on Insight Timer, talks, workshops and residential retreats, including a five-day programme at Hollyhock on Cortes Island that mixes guided sitting, nature walks, play, journaling and discussion away from devices. His recorded meditations tend to be gentle and experimental, inviting listeners to stop striving, rest in not knowing, or look honestly at how their screens shape their days.

courses.title: Reclaim Your Mind: Finding Rest and Play in a Wired World
courses.description: A five-day residential retreat at Hollyhock on Cortes Island about meeting technology with more choice and less guilt. Guided meditations, mindful walks, partner exercises, journaling and playful group work are all done without devices in the room.
courses.price: All-inclusive package (tuition, lodging and meals); price depends on accommodation and is shown at registration

free_resources.title: Doing Nothing At All
free_resources.description: A free guided practice of about twenty minutes on Insight Timer that invites you to put down the effort of self-improvement and simply be. It suits anyone whose meditation has started to feel like another task on the list.

free_resources.title: Screen Inquiry - Mindful Of Technology
free_resources.description: A longer guided reflection on your relationship with your devices. It looks at the physical and online spaces you spend time in and what they reveal about your habits and values.

free_resources.title: Calm Without Control
free_resources.description: A guided session working with sensations in the body to grow more at ease with uncertainty and discomfort. It is aimed at staying steady when circumstances are out of your hands.

free_resources.title: Stop Trying
free_resources.description: A short experiment in dropping the effort to meditate at all and letting whatever arises be as it is. Jay contrasts this with trying to do nothing, which still involves effort.
